draft.title: The development of human rights
card: Ideas of human rights grew slowly over many centuries. They were shaped by written documents and by campaigns that pushed for change.
Magna Carta
signed in England in 1215, it limited the power of the king. It supported the idea that rulers must follow the law, but it first protected mainly powerful nobles, not everyone.
18th-century declarations
the American Declaration of Independence (1776) and the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789) said people have rights that governments should respect.
Campaigns
people campaigned against slavery and for workers' rights and women's rights. These campaigns pushed the idea of rights to cover more people.
draft.remember: Human rights ideas grew from documents that limited rulers and from campaigns that widened who is protected.

a.q: What did Magna Carta contribute to the development of human rights?
opts: It supported the idea that rulers must follow the law
It gave equal rights to every person in England
It ended slavery across the British Empire
It created a court to enforce rights worldwide
a.why: Magna Carta limited the king's power and supported the idea that rulers are under the law. It is wrong to say it gave equal rights to all, because at first it mainly protected powerful nobles.
a.clue: Think about who it limited, and who it first protected.

b.q: Why did campaigns against slavery and for women's rights matter to the development of human rights?
opts: They pushed rights to cover people who had been left out
They replaced earlier documents such as Magna Carta
They were the first time anyone wrote about rights
They gave rulers new powers to decide who has rights
b.why: These campaigns challenged who was protected and pushed rights to include more people. They did not replace earlier documents, because ideas of rights grew through both documents and campaigns working over time.
b.clue: Ask who was missing from the early documents.

a.best: It supported the idea that rulers must follow the law

b.best: They pushed rights to cover people who had been left out

problems.detail: Magna Carta was not signed. King John agreed to it and it was sealed with his royal seal at Runnymede in 1215. Say 'sealed' or 'agreed to' instead of 'signed'.
